headline: Riyadh airport blast: Biman suspends Dhaka-Riyadh flights
summary: Flights BG339 and BG340 are grounded until further notice following an explosion at King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia.
details: An explosion at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has led to several injuries and disrupted flight operations.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights, specifically BG339 and BG340, until further notice.
The airline announced the decision in a statement on Saturday night, citing the total suspension of all flights from the airport.
Passengers already booked on these flights have been advised not to travel to the airport.
Biman is currently assessing the situation and promised to provide a detailed update on flight status and rescheduling on Sunday.
Affected passengers are encouraged to contact the airline's call center or visit the nearest Biman sales office for immediate assistance.
caption:

Affected passengers are encouraged to contact the airline's call center or visit the nearest Biman sales office for immediate assistance.

headline: Tarique Rahman calls sudden BNP parliamentary party meeting
summary: The meeting will discuss internal party discipline, law and order, constitutional amendments, and upcoming local government elections.
details: BNP's parliamentary party leader Tarique Rahman has called a sudden meeting of the party's parliamentary group.
The meeting is scheduled for Sunday at 6:00 PM at the government party's conference room in the National Parliament.
According to several senior party leaders, the agenda includes establishing internal party discipline and discussing the current law and order situation.
The leaders will also deliberate on constitutional amendments and the upcoming local government elections.
This meeting comes at a time when the date for the next parliamentary session has not yet been fixed.
caption:
Tarique Rahman has called an urgent meeting of the BNP parliamentary party to discuss discipline and elections.

BNP's parliamentary party leader Tarique Rahman has called a sudden meeting of the party's parliamentary group.

The meeting is scheduled for Sunday at 6:00 PM at the government party's conference room in the National Parliament.

According to several senior party leaders, the agenda includes establishing internal party discipline and discussing the current law and order situation.

The leaders will also deliberate on constitutional amendments and the upcoming local government elections.

This meeting comes at a time when the date for the next parliamentary session has not yet been fixed.
